question: Does the TCGA recount3 metadata expose an RNA-integrity field comparable to GTEx SMRIN, so RIN could span both cohorts and enter the cross-cohort GLM as an identifiable covariate?

gtex.note: Ranges are [min, median, max]. SMRIN = RNA integrity number (Bioanalyzer). SMTSISCH = ischemic time (minutes). Both fully populated.

tcga.note: a260_a280_ratio is a spectrophotometric PURITY ratio (protein/solvent contamination), not strand INTEGRITY (RIN). It is also absent from the GTEx metadata, so it is confounded in the opposite direction. No symmetric RNA-quality covariate exists across the two cohorts.

design_consequence: Every RIN-bearing sample is a GTEx normal; no TCGA sample (tumor or adjacent-normal) carries RIN. In the cross-cohort contrast (cell C/Cr) RIN is therefore perfectly collinear with the group indicator -> NON-IDENTIFIABLE as a design covariate. RIN/ischemic are carried into colData as DIAGNOSTIC-ONLY columns (report the GTEx-arm RIN distribution; optional low-RIN QC filter), never a GLM design term. RUVg latent factors are the sole confound corrector — robust and counts-only, exactly the graceful-degradation path plan risk #8 anticipated.
calibration_impact: The plan's RUVg+RIN-Cr calibration arm (B4, 'where the symmetry probe passed') is DROPPED — a non-identifiable term cannot be added to the design. The Stage-1 calibration matrix collapses to {recount3, xena-toil} x {naive-C, RUVg-Cr} vs the within-TCGA cell-A anchor.
